It is reported that Apple will launch its next-generation Apple Silicon chip, the M6, later this year. This article compiles all currently known information and explains why this generation holds particular significance in the Apple Silicon era.

M6 Specifications and Performance

According to a report from Bloomberg, Apple's M6 chip will feature several major upgrades over the current M5.

First, the M6 will adopt an updated memory architecture, delivering faster memory bandwidth. The current M5 has a maximum memory bandwidth of 153 GB per second.

The M6 is reported to boost memory bandwidth to 200 GB per second. Notably, the higher memory bandwidth of the M6 will enhance on-device AI performance.

The M6 chip will also comprehensively boost the processing speed of all cores and improve video encoding and decoding performance.

Bloomberg also reported that the M6 will feature a redesigned GPU. The current base M5 comes with up to 10 GPU cores, while the M6 is reported to feature up to 12 graphics processing cores, delivering smoother gaming experiences, faster video rendering, and improved performance in GPU-accelerated applications.

What Makes the M6 Different

However, the M6 will differ from all previous Apple Silicon chips in one major way.

Since the M1, Apple has consistently released higher-end "Pro" and "Max" configurations, and across the M1, M2, and M3 generations, it also released two "Ultra" chips.

This situation will change with the M6 generation. According to Mark Gurman, Apple will only release a base model M6 processor and will not release any higher-end Pro, Max, or Ultra versions.

Apple reportedly believes that the improvements in the M7 will be substantial enough to skip most of the M6 product lineup. The M7 is expected to bring larger upgrades in on-device AI processing capabilities, including support for memory bandwidth of up to 240 GB per second.

M6 Release Date and Products

The M6 chip is reported to debut as early as later this year. Apple has been testing the M6 in a new base-model MacBook Pro, which currently still comes with an M5 chip.

Whether the M6 chip will be used in other Apple products remains unknown. The base M7 is expected to launch in the first half of 2027, so most products will likely skip the M6 generation altogether.

What are your thoughts on Apple's upcoming M6 chip and this strategic shift? Do you think this is the right decision? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments below.
